summary.name: Graffiti / Street Art is a supplemental Drawing and Illustration design reference. The source does not name it as a directly named style in its collection.
summary.visualIdentity: Spray-painted lettering, tags, wall texture and street graphics share one coherent lettering style and palette. Overspray and layered paint are used selectively. Strokes are revealed, areas overpainted and layers replaced while the principal message stays recognizable.
summary.suitableUses: Explicit: lettering-focused pieces work alone. Supporting examples include music promos, event teasers, event promotions and culture explainers. Inferred fit: street-culture and urban subjects. Other topics are unspecified and need fit review.
summary.limitations: Source review covers only single frames at 1–8 seconds, with no continuous motion, sub-second timing, audio or later scenes. Color families are visual observations only. Random overspray and over-layering are excluded. Simulated paint is not physical production evidence. Remotion is a conditional fallback only.
summary.palette: Background policy is scene_dependent, and status is a style-compatible suggestion for new artwork without an approved palette. Direction: selected spray colors on a neutral wall. Illustrative tokens are background #E7E1D4, foreground #272631, accents #BC4861, #388A8B and #CEA248; they are not mandatory canvas colors. Foreground on background is 11.449:1, and accent_3 text is 6.312:1. Accent_1 and accent_2 are decorative fills only. Gradients are disabled. Task-approved colors override these tokens.
summary.motionAndInteraction: Motion is seeded spray reveals, overpaints and stroke movement, controlled by composition time. Use smooth authored movement where it helps. Keep deliberate sharp cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections and reading holds. Optional references: motion-037 (glyph release into a tag language) and motion-038 (punctuation zoom). Motion-012 and motion-015 suit chapters or narrative steps. Use references only when scene assets support them. Interactive behavior is unspecified.
summary.audio: No audio is fixed by this style. Music synchronization may suit promos, but reveals should not depend on audio alone and beats need measured audio analysis. Voiceover, sound effects, ambience or silence are chosen from the topic. Explicit task audio is honored; if absent, propose a coherent direction and state assumptions. Speech must stay intelligible, and no audio assets are invented.
summary.assetRequirements: No uploads are required. Exact copy and any approved palette come from the task. Prepare tags and main lettering as separate seeded assets, and load local fonts before rendering. Inspect glyph or mark geometry before using motion references. Do not invent copy or brand marks. Record missing assets rather than substituting them.
summary.combinations: style-105 suits beat-synced spray reveals: use the primary spray palette only, keep the message readable, avoid a stroke on every beat and avoid random overspray. style-054 suits zine flyer cutaways: flyers use the primary palette, the wall stays the main scene, and mixed palettes or photocopy noise are avoided. Lettering-only pieces need no hybrid.
summary.productionApproach: HyperFrames is the default pipeline: use data-composition-id, data-width/height, data-duration, clip timing and one paused GSAP timeline registered in window.__timelines, then run its check, snapshot and render commands. Canvas 2D and SVG draw the spray and marks. GSAP owns motion. Motion is optional for DOM/SVG only after seek checks. chroma-js is optional for contrast checks. Remotion is fallback only.
